about: English meaning written for this library (en-scriptures): line by line, plain and faithful to the words, from the words themselves, their grammar and the dictionaries (Monier-Williams, Apte); not copied from any source. [meaning, [footnotes]]

shanti.1: We pray for that happiness and welfare: a clear way for the sacrifice,
a clear way for the lord of the sacrifice. May divine well-being be ours;
well-being to human beings. May the healing remedy rise high.
May there be happiness for our two-footed, happiness for the four-footed.
m01: The Puruṣa is thousand-headed, thousand-eyed, thousand-footed.
Enveloping the earth on every side, he stood ten fingers' breadth beyond it.
m02: The Puruṣa alone is all this — what has been and what is to be.
He is lord of immortality too, since he grows higher by food.
m03: Such is his greatness, and the Puruṣa is greater still than this.
All beings are one quarter of him; three quarters of him are the immortal in heaven.
m04: The three-quartered Puruṣa rose on high; a quarter of him came to be here again.
From there he spread out on every side, over what eats and what does not eat (the living and the lifeless).
m05: From him Virāj was born, and from Virāj the Puruṣa.
Once born, he reached beyond the earth, behind it and before it.
m06: When the gods spread out the sacrifice with the Puruṣa as the oblation,
spring was its ghee, summer its fuel, autumn its oblation.
m07: Seven were its enclosing sticks, and thrice seven fuel-sticks were made,
when the gods, spreading out the sacrifice, bound the Puruṣa as the victim.
m08: On the sacred grass they sprinkled and consecrated him, the sacrifice — the Puruṣa born first of all.
With him the gods sacrificed, and so did the Sādhyas, a class of celestial beings, and the seers who were there.
m09: From that sacrifice in which all was offered, the ghee mixed with curds was gathered.
He made those animals that live in the air, and those of the forest and those of the village.
m10: From that sacrifice in which all was offered, the Ṛk verses and the Sāman chants were born;
the metres were born from it; the Yajus was born from it.
m11: From it horses were born, and all those that have teeth in both jaws;
cows too were born from it; from it goats and sheep were born.
m12: When they divided the Puruṣa, into how many parts did they fashion him?
What was his mouth, what his two arms? What are his two thighs and his two feet called?
m13: The Brāhmaṇa was his mouth; the Rājanya, the Kṣatriya, was made his two arms;
his two thighs were that which is the Vaiśya; from his two feet the Śūdra was born.
m14: The moon was born from the mind, the sun was born from the eye;
from the mouth Indra and Agni, and from the breath Vāyu was born.
m15: From the navel came the mid-air, from the head the sky came forth;
from the feet the earth, from the ear the quarters; so they fashioned the worlds.
m16: I know this great Puruṣa, the colour of the sun, beyond darkness,
when he, the wise one, having set all forms apart and made their names, abides calling them by those names.
m17: He whom Dhātṛ, the ordainer, proclaimed in the beginning, whom Indra knew well in the four quarters —
One who knows him thus becomes immortal here; there is no other path to go by.
m18: By the sacrifice the gods worshipped the Sacrifice; those were the first ordinances.
Those mighty ones reach the heaven where the Sādhyas, the gods of old, dwell.
m19: He arose from the waters and from the earth's essence, and came forth from Viśvakarman.
Tvaṣṭṛ, the divine craftsman, goes on shaping his form; that, in the beginning, was the whole birth of the Puruṣa.
m20: I know this great Puruṣa, the colour of the sun, beyond darkness.
One who knows him thus becomes immortal here; there is no other path to go by.
m21: Prajāpati moves within the womb; unborn, he is born in many ways.
The wise know his source fully; the creators long for the station of Marīci and the other seers.
m22: He who shines for the gods, who is the priest of the gods,
who was born before the gods — salutations to the radiant, holy one.
m23: Bringing forth the radiant, holy one, the gods said this in the beginning:
The Brāhmaṇa who knows you thus — the gods shall be in his power.
m24: Hrī (modesty) and Lakṣmī are your two wives; day and night are your two flanks;
the stars are your form; the two Aśvins are your open mouth.
Wish for me what is desired; wish for me that (world) yonder; wish for me everything.
shanti.end: We pray for that happiness and welfare: a clear way for the sacrifice,
a clear way for the lord of the sacrifice. May divine well-being be ours;
well-being to human beings. May the healing remedy rise high.
May there be happiness for our two-footed, happiness for the four-footed.

m02: The line is also read: he is lord of immortality and of what grows by food.
m05: Paścād bhūmim atho puraḥ is also read: then he made the earth, and then the bodies (of beings).
m21: Marīcīnām is also read as 'of the rays of light': the creators long for the station of the rays.
